source.installedFrom: a local candidate tarball, NOT the public registry
source.versionCaveat: version is what the package declares. It does not identify these bytes: a local candidate shares the version string of the published release, so read specifier and integrity for identity.

purpose: Composition records for sections the convergence project has migrated. A record LINKS the authorities that own each fact; it does not restate them.
rules: identity names a composition declared in pattern-map.json, which owns composition identity and its local-or-shared disposition. That disposition is an owner decision and is deliberately absent here.
packageExport is false for every website-local composition. A record that claimed otherwise would advertise something consumers cannot install.
refs point at real files. A ref into the website repository is marked repo: website and is cited, not resolved, because this checkout cannot see it.

dependsOn ids are the names their authority uses: a component id is the name src/index.ts exports, a contract id is the contract's own id. The earlier record used lowercase labels that matched neither, and nothing checked them.

limitations: Nine compositions, not eleven. pattern-map.json declares CMP-01..CMP-11; CMP-05 (PostCard) has no record of its own because it is part of writing-teaser rather than a separable composition, and CMP-09 (Ticker) has none because NO batch migrated it - it imports neither a component nor a token. Their absence is stated here so it cannot be read as an oversight, and neither may be counted as adoption.

Four of these nine use NO design-system COMPONENT: chrome-footer, work, speaking and the Ticker that has no record at all. What was migrated in those sections is tokens, spacing floors and the shared destination record. Each says so in its own localExceptions rather than leaving a reader to infer component adoption from the presence of a record.
A record describes relationships, not appearance. It does not and cannot say a section looks right; that is what the four owner-accepted batch reviews are for.
packageExport is false for every record here. These are website compositions; none is installable, and none of them is an external consumer of the package.

These records make no backlog claim, though the work section does produce the tall mobile rows tracked as F24. ref.backlog is not in record-ownership.json's claimToFact, and adding an unmapped claim kind is exactly what that registry exists to prevent; the batch C decisions record owns that finding instead.

A composition's dependency on the shared destination record is claimed as ref.source on destinations.ts, not as a dependsOn entry. dependsOn recognises components and contracts, which are package facts; a website module is route-and-content, and claiming it twice would put one fact under two authorities.
